name: Scientific socialism
summary: Scientific socialism is the Marx-Engels doctrine that socialism is the outcome of the historical development of production, not a moral blueprint, and that its basis is the materialist conception of history. It holds that capitalism's social production under private ownership produces crises and a proletariat, which takes political power, turns the means of production into public property and replaces market anarchy with a social plan, after which classes and eventually the state fade away.
scope: The founding theory of Marx and Engels, centred on Engels's Socialism: Utopian and Scientific (1880) and the Communist Manifesto (1848), with Engels's 1895 introduction on tactics. It excludes later Leninist, Stalinist and Maoist doctrines that adopted the label, and the reformist and libertarian strands; questions the founders never faced are inferred from core principles and marked low confidence.

keyFigures.name: Karl Marx
keyFigures.role: Co-founder; developer of the materialist conception of history and the critique of capitalist political economy.

sources.usedFor: Exploitation, ideology, religion, the Commune model of recallable officials on workers' pay, and communism's higher stage.

sources.title: Socialism: Utopian and Scientific, chapter 3 (historical materialism and the proletarian revolution)
sources.author: Friedrich Engels (1880)
sources.usedFor: Materialist conception of history, anarchy of commodity production, class state, public ownership, planning and the withering of the state.

sources.title: Manifesto of the Communist Party, chapter 2: Proletarians and Communists
sources.author: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels (1848)
sources.usedFor: Abolition of bourgeois property, wage labour, family, nationality, the ten measures and proletarian rule.

sources.title: Introduction to Marx's The Class Struggles in France
sources.author: Friedrich Engels (1895)
sources.usedFor: Universal suffrage, legality, the limits of barricade fighting and mass rather than minority revolution.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Engels calls commodity production anarchic and says its crises show the mode of production in revolt against the mode of exchange; social planning is meant to replace the market.

public-ownership.rationale: Engels says the proletariat seizes political power and turns the means of production into public property, with state takeover of big industry as the first step.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The Manifesto lists a heavy progressive income tax among the measures for advanced countries.

unions-good.rationale: Engels treats organised workers as the force that builds class power, but the founders also saw unions as defensive and limited unless tied to the aim of abolishing wage labour.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Manifesto sums up the theory in one sentence: abolition of private (bourgeois) property.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Engels notes trusts and joint-stock companies socialise production while remaining capitalist, so regulation is at best a stopgap; the aim is public control, not tidier capitalism.

strong-leader.rationale: Engels insists the revolution must be made by masses who understand their aims, not by a minority or an individual commander.

state-harmful.rationale: Engels expects the state to wither away only after classes vanish, and the proletarian state is needed in the meantime; so not unnecessary now, though it is a class tool.

limit-guns.rationale: No stated position; Engels' view that workers may someday need arms conflicts with ordinary regulation, so adherents are split.

empower-police-military.rationale: The state's armed bodies are the ruling class's instrument in this view, so strengthening them is opposed under capitalism.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The Manifesto calls prostitution a product of bourgeois family and property, but no legal stance is given.

decide-locally.rationale: The Manifesto favours state centralisation in proletarian hands, while the later Commune model stressed local bodies; no clear split-free answer.

traditional-family.rationale: The Manifesto expects the bourgeois family to vanish with capital and attacks it as resting on private gain.

more-religion-public.rationale: Religion is treated as an ideological reflex of material conditions that fades as they change, so a bigger public role is opposed.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The Manifesto says social conditions shape the family and relations between the sexes, which supports a social account of gender roles.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Manifesto says working men have no country and that national differences are fading under the world market.

gradual-change.rationale: Engels sees socialism as a leap from the old order through the proletariat taking power, not a slow reform of existing institutions.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The founders favoured international working-class unity, but nothing about interstate bodies like the UN.

free-trade.rationale: The Manifesto sees free trade as serving the bourgeoisie while hastening revolution; it is not a benefit to all.

nation-first.rationale: The Manifesto holds that national antagonisms are vanishing and workers' emancipation needs united action across countries.

limit-growth.rationale: Engels sees abundant production as the basis for abolishing classes, so limiting growth cuts against the theory.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Productive forces make socialism possible, but Engels says the problem is the social form of ownership, not technology itself.

revolution-justified.rationale: Engels describes the proletarian revolution as the way the working class takes power and converts the means of production into public property.

experts-over-public.rationale: The movement claims scientific knowledge, but Engels stresses mass understanding and the working class acting for itself.

central-planning.rationale: Engels says society can replace production's anarchy with a social plan once it controls the productive forces.

socialized-markets.rationale: Commodity production is the root of anarchy in Engels' account, so keeping markets even under social ownership would be foreign to the theory.

land-value-tax.rationale: The Manifesto wants land ownership abolished and rents used publicly, not a single-tax reform leaving capital and wages intact.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The Manifesto lists the abolition of the right of inheritance among its measures.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The Manifesto calls free trade a force of capitalist development; protection is a bourgeois device, though neither is the workers' answer.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The Manifesto calls for state-owned factories and production under a common plan, which includes steering investment.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The Manifesto says industry is already destroying small property and the goal is common ownership of the means of production.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The Manifesto aims to end appropriation under which the worker lives only to increase capital, abolishing wage labour as a relation.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The Manifesto wants credit centralised in a state bank, the opposite of abolishing central banks.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Founders reject class collaboration and see employers and workers as opposed classes.

one-party-rule.rationale: Engels sees the party as a mass movement acting within legal channels; the single ruling party is a later Leninist development.

democracy-best.rationale: The Manifesto says the first step is winning the battle of democracy, but democracy is a means in a class struggle, not an end in itself.

workers-councils.rationale: Mixed: Marx praised the Paris Commune as a working body replacing parliamentarism, but Engels's 1895 introduction relies on universal suffrage and electoral work.

natural-rulers.rationale: The theory treats ruling classes as products of economic arrangements, not natural superiority.

political-violence-never.rationale: Engels presents revolution as a historical necessity and does not rule out force.

war-builds-character.rationale: Founders saw wars as ruling-class affairs fought at workers' expense.

separate-church-state.rationale: Marxists favour removing religion from state power and treat faith as a private matter.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Engels treats ideas of right as products of economic conditions, not divine revelation.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Courts and arms are organs of the class state; privatising them would hand the ruling class direct control.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Manifesto dismisses national distinctions as fading and sets class above nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Manifesto opens by saying the history of all hitherto existing society is the history of class struggles, and Engels grounds this in modes of production.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The aim is abolition of classes and later distribution by need, though the founders disliked treating equality as an abstract demand.

civilizational-union.rationale: The Manifesto bases solidarity on class, not on shared civilization or religion.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Founders attack the bourgeois reduction of social relations to cash payment and naked self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The founders mocked bourgeois rights but did not subordinate persons to duties; the free development of each is the condition for all.

limit-population.rationale: Engels treats poverty as arising from social arrangements, not numbers, so coercive limits are not favoured.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Engels treats industry as creating the conditions for socialism, even while capitalism misuses it.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Productive forces developing against capitalist forms drive history, though the aim is social control, not speed itself.

restore-past-order.rationale: The Manifesto treats the past order as vanishing for good and as based on class domination.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Scientific socialism claims a theory of history guiding action, so judging policy without the theory goes against the method.

direct-action.rationale: Engels urged patient mass organisation, using elections and parliament, over premature direct clashes.

means-match-ends.rationale: The Manifesto accepts despotic inroads on property as means; the end does not have to be mirrored in the method.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Engels sees development of production as what makes classless society possible.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Engels expects the distinction between town and country and the old division of labour to end under the planned association.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Production by social plan to meet community needs, with classes abolished, leads to distribution by need.

production-for-use.rationale: Engels contrasts anarchic production for exchange with planned production for the needs of the community.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Manifesto says capital is appropriated through wage labour that gives workers only a bare subsistence while capital grows.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Manifesto calls for the proletariat to be raised to the ruling class and to make despotic inroads on bourgeois property until class distinctions disappear (s3).

collective-farming.rationale: The Manifesto wants industrial armies, a common plan for agriculture and waste lands, so collective farming follows, though peasants were handled cautiously.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Engels sees capitalist competition and crises as unavoidable, but the exact war thesis is later Marxist theory.

taxation-theft.rationale: The Manifesto demands a heavy progressive tax, so taxation is a legitimate tool.

harm-principle.rationale: The Manifesto accepts despotic inroads on property, which breach a strict harm limit.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Manifesto treats rights as class-shaped and aims at an association in which the free development of each depends on all.

conscription.rationale: The Manifesto lists industrial armies and Engels accepted a citizens' militia, but no clear stance on conscription.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The Manifesto puts winning democracy first and class power over individual exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Engels says the state is a capitalist machine, not a firm serving customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Engels describes socialism as humanity's leap from necessity into freedom through mastery of its own social conditions.

media-academia-power.rationale: The Manifesto sees economic class power, not universities or media, as the real basis of political power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The theory explains social difference by economic conditions rather than inborn racial traits.

organic-representation.rationale: The class-based theory rejects corporate representation through families and trade bodies cutting across class conflict.

total-state.rationale: Engels expects the state to wither away; a state directing all of life, including culture, is not the goal.

national-rebirth.rationale: The founders see nations as secondary to class and decadence stories as ideological.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The Manifesto opposes national rivalry among workers and the exploitation of one nation by another.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The Manifesto treats feudal ties as a past order swept away by the bourgeoisie.

bound-labor.rationale: The Manifesto describes the feudal bonds of serfdom as swept away by capitalism, and the goal is workers' freedom.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Ruling ideas are those of the ruling class, but scientific socialism also claims its own account is objective, so adherents tension.

universal-morality.rationale: Engels says ideas of right and justice come from each era's economics, not timeless reason.

single-common-good.rationale: The theory holds that society is divided into classes with opposed interests, so a single common good is a ruling-class claim until classes disappear.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Once workers hold the means of production, they govern production, and Engels sees the producers' association replacing capitalist command.

school-vouchers.rationale: The Manifesto wants free public education for all children, not vouchers into private schooling.

economic-freedom.rationale: The Manifesto sees bourgeois freedom of trade and capital as freedom for owners, and abolishes bourgeois property.

rule-by-example.rationale: Political power is the organised power of one class, not moral example from rulers.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Workers have no country, so benefits tied to citizenship cut against internationalism.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The Manifesto requires equal work from all, but conditional benefits under capitalism target workers.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Manifesto sets bourgeoisie and proletariat as opposed classes in struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not a founders' concern; the theory takes over the gains of earlier development and sees ruling ideas as reflecting class.

workers-nation.rationale: The Manifesto says workers have no country and calls for united action of leading countries.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Manifesto attacks the bourgeois family and expects its roles to vanish.

ban-interest.rationale: The Manifesto centralises credit in a state bank rather than outlawing lending.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The theory is hostile to divisions among workers and rooted in class, not race.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Engels says the state is the organ of the economically dominant class, in the modern case essentially a capitalist machine.

elite-replacement.rationale: The theory explains migration by capitalism's world market rather than a plot.

national-mission.rationale: The theory rejects national missions in favour of international class solidarity.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The Manifesto says the bourgeois family treats the wife as a mere instrument of production.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The Manifesto says the state manages the bourgeoisie's common affairs, so elites serve class interests.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Manifesto wants a state that organises production, not one limited to defence and property.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Racial purity is foreign to a theory built on class and internationalism.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The Manifesto says united action of at least the leading civilised countries is a first condition of emancipation.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Religious taboos are treated as ideology, not a basis for law.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Engels expects the state to wither away; encirclement doctrine is later Leninist-Stalinist.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Manifesto calls for winning democracy but treats legitimacy as a class matter.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist aim is a bourgeois state policy, not a workers' goal.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Engels accepts revolutionary force and does not hold to a non-aggression rule.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Engels treats competition as producing anarchy and crises, while class struggle, not individual rivalry, is the motor.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Engels says the ruling parties of order are destroyed by the legality they created; banning parties is the ruling class's move against workers.

separated-powers.rationale: Not a founders' principle; the Commune model unites legislative and executive work.

vanguard-party.rationale: Engels favoured a mass party and mass understanding; the disciplined vanguard is Leninist.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The movement aims at the proletariat, the poorest class, as the ruling class.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Engels treats organised worker action as the source of working-class power.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Engels locates poverty in capitalist production and the reserve army, not numbers.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Class, not ethnicity, is the main division in the theory.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The Manifesto accepts despotic inroads in the transition, though liberties for workers are valued.

party-controls-media.rationale: Engels relies on open political agitation by the party and press.

party-commands-army.rationale: Engels argued that the party should work to win the army's rank and file; command by a party is a later theory.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Marx praised the Commune's workman's wage for officials, according to the SEP discussion of elected, recallable officials.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Engels prized organisation and unity in the party, though binding discipline is formalised later.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The founders supported democratic republic and rejected monarchic prerogative.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Clerical hierarchies are part of the ruling ideology the theory opposes.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The Manifesto offers no moral-censorship programme.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The founders left term limits to the form of democratic government and gave no principle either way; the Commune model stressed recall instead.

recall-officials.rationale: Marx's Commune model, as SEP presents it, has elected officials recallable at any time.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The Manifesto calls for gradually abolishing the distinction between town and country, and treats industry as the force that builds the working class.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National questions are secondary to class in the Manifesto, and neither text offers a rule on reunifying states divided by outside powers.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Engels grades societies by stage of economic development, so cultures are not simply different.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Engels presents socialism as science and the materialist view of nature and history against religious accounts.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The Manifesto ties the bourgeois family to private gain but puts forward no legal restriction of this kind.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Religion is treated as a private matter, not a ground for exemption from general laws.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Political forms follow economic structure, so formal independence without a change in property relations leaves class rule in place.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Winning democracy is a first step, but no stance on assemblies for rewriting constitutions.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The theory aims at freedom, but accepts despotic inroads on property.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The Manifesto wants credit centralised in a state bank under proletarian control, not independent of it.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The Manifesto wants property transformed into common ownership, a stronger version of this claim.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Engels warned that state ownership does not itself abolish capital, but the Soviet case postdates him and adherents are split.

collective-defense.rationale: The theory opposes bourgeois alliance blocs and national war aims.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Manifesto era Marxists favoured subordinating church to civil power; the Commune later disestablished it.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Founders saw no neutral stance above class in state power.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not covered; the founders did not address special regions, but flexibility in transition is consistent.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Engels treats religion and divine right as ideological reflections of class rule.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The Manifesto lists a heavy progressive income tax.

character-from-environment.rationale: The Manifesto says people's ideas change with material conditions, and Engels grounds ideas in the economy.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The founders preferred accountable democratic bodies.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Founders rejected balancing classes in a constitution.

leader-cult.rationale: Engels stressed mass understanding over reliance on individual leaders.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Engels expects class antagonism to end once the means of production become public property; the claim is a later Maoist development.

land-redistribution.rationale: The Manifesto turns land rents to public purposes and wants a common plan, not private parcels for farmers.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The Manifesto sets class above nation and denies national antagonisms.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Religion is a private and fading ideology, so punishing leaving it is opposed.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The Manifesto prioritises class over ethnic or linguistic kinship.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Engels states that the final causes of social change lie in modes of production and exchange, not in philosophy or ideas of justice; this is the core of the doctrine.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The Manifesto says national seclusion has given way to universal interdependence through the world market, and socialism is an international movement.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Engels's 1895 introduction says the era of minority surprise attacks is over and revolution needs the conscious mass behind it.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Manifesto lists abolition of the right of inheritance among its measures and seeks the end of class privilege.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Manifesto says the working men have no country and calls for abolishing nationality, so nationalist schooling is opposed.

public-money-creation.rationale: Measure 5 of the Manifesto centralises credit in the hands of the state by a national bank with state capital.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Engels holds that the contradiction between social production and private appropriation produces crises that lead to proletarian revolution rather than permanent adaptation.

elective-rulers.rationale: Marx's Commune model has officials elected, recallable and on workers' pay.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Engels in 1895 praised universal suffrage and parliamentary strength, and the Commune was a working body, not a monarch's.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The Manifesto attacks bourgeois philanthropists and charity as conservative socialism that leaves the system alone.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Marx held the ruling ideas of an epoch are those of the ruling class, with religion and ideology serving to reconcile people to the order.

native-born-offices.rationale: The Manifesto says working men have no country and calls for abolishing national antagonisms.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Class, not ancestry, is the political category in the Manifesto.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The Commune model abolished the standing army in favour of the armed people, and the Manifesto treats the state as a class instrument.

office-by-exam.rationale: Marx held up the Commune model in which officials are elected, recallable and paid workers wages, against a separate bureaucratic caste.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The Commune model Marx praised made delegates revocable at any time and bound by their electors.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Public ownership of the means of production and social planning replace private provision; private accounts are capitalist finance.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The first measure in the Manifesto is abolition of property in land and application of rent to public purposes, so land is public rather than private.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Engels in 1895 endorses universal suffrage and parliamentary use by workers, so parliamentary control of spending is compatible, though the Commune was a working body.

corporate-influence.rationale: Engels calls the modern state the capitalists' state, an instrument of the owning class, so business power over government is expected rather than an aberration.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The Manifesto says bourgeois jurisprudence is merely the will of the ruling class made into law, so law as such carries no binding authority.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Historical materialism explains politics through classes and modes of production, not secret plots by an ethnic or religious minority.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The Manifesto sets out the abolition of the bourgeois family and the property basis of marriage, though it speaks of abolishing the family more than of repealing marriage law.

informal-organisation.rationale: Engels's 1895 introduction stresses mass organisation and the party's electoral and organised growth, not small informal cells.

religious-nation.rationale: The Manifesto says working men have no country and that national differences are vanishing, and Marx treats religion as ideology; neither addresses defining a nation by religion.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The Manifesto says communism abolishes bourgeois property in the means of production, not the personal appropriation of the products of labour.

defeat-communism.rationale: Its adherents are communists who aim to abolish capitalist property, so defeating communism is the opposite of their aim.

religion-illusion.rationale: Marx treated religion as an illusory consolation for real suffering that ends when the conditions needing illusion are abolished.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The Manifesto credits the bourgeoisie with creating enormous productive forces and the proletariat, the basis of socialism.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The founders tie women's subordination to the property-based family and the economic order, so equality requires transforming the economy.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Engels's contrast between scientific and utopian socialism rejects small communal experiments as a route to socialism, in favour of class struggle and social ownership at the scale of society.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Scientific socialism is a communist doctrine that holds capitalism must be overcome by communism.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The founders left little on this; their materialist critique of bourgeois morality and the family points against criminal penalties, though period attitudes were mixed.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The proletarian state is a class dictatorship that suppresses the old ruling class, but the founders favoured the democratic republic and universal suffrage as the route to power.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Marx and Engels treated religion as ideology arising from social conditions and opposed state religion, so civil punishment of blasphemy has no place.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The founders condemned bourgeois colonial exploitation as part of capitalism's expansion that socialism would end.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The Manifesto speaks of winning the battle of democracy and associated producers; direct participation in workplaces is an inference, not a stated programme.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The doctrine holds class to be the fundamental division and the driver of history, with other oppressions derived from it rather than coequal.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The Manifesto and Engels place politics in the struggle between proletariat and bourgeoisie, which they treat as irreconcilable; the left-right framing itself is later.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marx's theory of alienated labour under capitalism is a core part of his account of wage labour, as Stanford's entry sets out.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Marx and Engels hold that authority and the state arise from class relations of production, not from God.

social-market-economy.rationale: The doctrine seeks to replace market anarchy with social planning, not to temper the market.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The Manifesto calls for arming the proletariat and the founders looked to a revolution defended by force; the standing armies of states are to wither with the state.

rich-first.rationale: The doctrine aims at abolishing class and private ownership of production, not letting some grow rich first.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Marx and Engels wanted to abolish class rule and championed a republic; the Manifesto treats hereditary privilege as a feature of old class society.

property-franchise.rationale: The Manifesto calls winning the battle of democracy the first step of the proletarian revolution, which needs universal suffrage rather than property qualifications.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Engels linked the family and women's subordination to property relations and Marx described capitalism as exhausting soil and worker; the explicit link is later Marxist-feminist and eco-Marxist work.

reification.rationale: Marx's analysis of commodity fetishism in Capital says social relations among producers appear as relations between things; Engels's text sees economic forces ruling people before socialism.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The Manifesto holds that the ruling ideas are those of the ruling class, and Marx held bourgeois freedom of the press to be class-limited.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Marx and Engels used bourgeois legality tactically and also called for revolutionary dictatorship of the proletariat, so adherents split on binding rulers to standing laws.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Manifesto says the workers have no country and rejects nationalism; the proletariat is a class defined by position, not race.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The Manifesto treats religion as bourgeois ideology and favours secular marriage; legal restrictions on marriage by religion contradict its universalist outlook.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Scientific socialism is internationalist and class-based and treats such sectarian divisions as tools that divide workers.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Manifesto describes capital as concentrating in few hands and bourgeois domination over politics, which socialism aims to end, though the founders frame it as class power rather than liberty.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Manifesto and Engels hold that private appropriation of what wage workers produce is the source of exploitation, so income should follow labour rather than ownership.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Engels's tactics essay and the Manifesto treat revolutionary force as legitimate when needed and accept that the proletariat may have to fight, so an absolute ban on killing is foreign to the doctrine.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Manifesto says national differences are already vanishing under capitalism and treats nationality as a historical product, not an eternal essence.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The Manifesto treats nationality and religion as bourgeois ideology to be superseded, so honouring national martyrs as saints is alien to it.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Historical materialism explains politics through class interests and modes of production, and Marx treats religious and moral language as ideology.

culture-before-state.rationale: Engels holds that the final causes of social change lie in modes of production and exchange, not in ideas, so cultural renewal does not precede political change.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The Manifesto replaces national and minority rivalries with class and says the workers have no country, so economic control by a national majority is not an aim.

independent-unions.rationale: Marx and Engels valued unions as schools of class struggle run by workers, but did not treat independence from a future workers' state.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The proletariat seizes political power and turns the means of production into public property; socialism without it is not what the theory describes.

municipal-property.rationale: Engels says the proletariat takes the means of production into public property through the state, not into local community ownership.

family-wage.rationale: Marx criticised the slogan of a fair day's wage and aimed to abolish the wage system itself.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The materialist conception of history grounds society in production, treating religion and ideas as products of material conditions.

racial-group-interests.rationale: History is class struggle, and workers have no country; organising by race cuts across class.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The founders backed some wars and revolutionary wars; adherents are split and they never set a general rule.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Marx and Engels held that workers have no country and that class, not language, is the decisive division; the founders never made language the test of nationhood.

free-public-college.rationale: The Manifesto demands free education for all children in public schools, which points toward free public higher education, though universities were not named.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The Commune model replaced the standing army with the armed people, so a state-only monopoly on arms is not endorsed.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The Commune showed the workers cannot just take over the ready-made state machine; Engels in 1895 still counts on winning power by suffrage, so adherents are split toward agreement.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Socialism rests on one social plan replacing market anarchy, not on competing experiments.

sacred-nation.rationale: The Manifesto holds that workers have no country and that national differences fade, rejecting the nation as sacred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Marx's species-being sits alongside the view that human nature is historically formed by social relations, so the sources support neither side clearly.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Marx treats religion as ideology tied to class society and not as a shared truth, and expected it to fade with socialism.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Manifesto has communists organise the proletariat into a class and a political party, and Engels's 1895 introduction stresses the party's mass electoral work.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The founders backed women's equality but the Manifesto's ten measures abolish inheritance and land rent, so equal inheritance is not their programme; split.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The Commune model has officials elected, recallable and on workers' pay, and the Manifesto abolishes feudal and class privilege.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Engels saw universal suffrage as a means for workers to gain strength, but held that the state expresses the ruling class, so democracy depends on class content, not procedure alone.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The Manifesto says communists can sum up their theory as the abolition of private property, so first-come ownership of land is contrary to it.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: The founders never addressed international criminal courts; Marx treated courts and law as expressions of class power, but also opposed aggressive wars, so the answer is split.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Engels and Marx treated religion as ideology reflecting material conditions and rejected literal divine revelation.

national-church-status.rationale: The Manifesto treats religion as a bourgeois-era ideology and holds no state church could be privileged in a proletarian order.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The Manifesto says the working men have no country, and Marx and Engels treat national attachments as products of bourgeois conditions.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The Manifesto holds that workers' interests are international and cross national lines, so kin ties to compatriots abroad carry no weight.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The Manifesto says constant revolutionising of production dissolves old and venerable prejudices and relations, so a return to ancestral values is rejected.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Engels and Marx judged distribution by the relations of production and exploitation, and called for abolishing bourgeois property, not for defending fortunes gained by exchange.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Marx and Engels held that value is created by labour, the foundation of their account of exploitation and surplus value.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The Manifesto says workers have no country and calls for abolishing nationality as a division, though it also treats the proletariat as national in form.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: They expected a proletarian state to abolish commodity production, so a market economy is not socialism; party-led market socialism was not envisaged.

missingStatements.text: Social and political change is driven mainly by changes in how society produces and exchanges goods, not by ideas or moral insight.
missingStatements.rationale: Engels states that the final causes of social change lie in modes of production and exchange, not in philosophy or ideas of justice; this is the core of the doctrine.

missingStatements.text: Socialism should be pursued as the outcome of a scientific study of society's historical development rather than as an ideal blueprint of a just society.
missingStatements.rationale: Engels contrasts scientific socialism with utopian schemes, saying it bases itself on historical conditions rather than on abstract ideals.
missingStatements.declined: Self-description of method (science versus utopia) that no other ideology would answer against; its substance is carried by material-conditions-drive-history and reason-over-faith.

missingStatements.text: Production should be regulated by a single social plan rather than left to competing producers.
missingStatements.rationale: Engels says society, once in control of the productive forces, replaces anarchy of production with a planned, socially regulated production.

notes: Adherents differ on how far Engels's 1895 emphasis on legal, electoral methods holds against his earlier view of revolution; answers on revolution follow the main line of both texts. The label was later claimed by Leninist and other regimes, which would answer party, army and state questions differently.
